comment: No source is published. Two faults, both checkable. First, three of the four jacks are dead: process reads the first input only, so the coherence, duration and duration-coherence jacks are configured, drawn on the panel and never read. Second, the five outputs are each one distribution away from the name on the jack. The distribution function subtracts one from the number it is given before dispatching, so 1 to 5 are Cauchy, logistic, hyperbolic, arcsine and exponential and anything else falls through to a uniform draw. Wander calls it with 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 for the five outputs. The result is that the Cauchy jack carries a uniform draw and the exponential distribution never appears on any jack. The same function is called once more with the duration switch's own value, and that call is not shifted, which is what says the five output calls are the ones that are wrong. The rate knob is configured 0.01 to 20 but is clamped at 4, so four fifths of its travel does nothing; the step length can still push the rate above 4 afterwards. Both coherence controls are named for different distributions but only the amplitude one is used: it is the shape parameter for all six draws, including the duration one.
